parts.title: A Shared Storytelling World
parts.intro: A film seen with a parent can lead, years later, to a search for a book. We begin with that small journey, then meet writers whose people and words have found lives in print, performance and broadcasting. The question running through these pages is simple: what helps a story reach someone, and what helps its maker continue?

parts.title: Songs and Voices
parts.intro: A melody can leave the theatre with us. Inside it are words someone chose, a tune someone shaped and a voice that made them intimate. These lives bring us closer to the shared work within songs we may already love.

parts.title: Films and Filmmakers
parts.intro: The voices now meet a screen. A household, a village, a child’s imagination: each becomes a world people make together. The history gives us our bearings; the films and lives that follow let us stay with the choices, friendships and labour behind a finished work.

parts.title: Memory and Discovery
parts.intro: A screening ends. A film’s life need not. Materials kept in a home, a collection entrusted to another person, a question pursued through an archive: these acts can bring a story within reach again. Remembering is work that another generation may one day depend on.

parts.title: A New Search for Stories
parts.intro: The written story returns to the centre of our journey. Gourahari Das’s Bapa inspired Pratikshya. A different encounter, in Malkangiri, leads towards DAMaN. These beginnings let us look behind recognition and meet people deciding that a story was worth the work.

explore.label: Explore Bara Badhu, Maliput Melodies, Ananta and Madhumallati

parts.title: Changing Screens
parts.intro: A story can enter a home at a familiar hour, or wait for someone to choose it on a phone. Television and streaming change the occasions for watching. The need for writing, performance and an audience remains.

parts.title: Making the Next Film Possible
parts.intro: Affection for a film can become a ticket bought, a book sought out, a new collaboration. Sustaining that possibility also requires money to return to the people doing the work. We close by asking how makers, audiences and public institutions can help a good beginning become continuing creative life.
